scope: Lead-major, time-minor patch layout and encoder/decoder positional indexing
Visible-only encoder selection and decoder restoration with different masks per batch item
Masked patch loss compared independently with a masked raw-sample MSE
Prediction-path input Jacobian: zero at hidden input samples, nonzero at visible samples
Finite, nonzero gradients and actual parameter updates in the full pilot model
Train/eval inference consistency and inference batch-size consistency
Optimizer/scheduler order, train/validation separation, frozen linear probe and checkpoint replay

previous_initialization_issue.observation: Historical TransformerEncoder layers began with identical values, but separate parameter storage.
previous_initialization_issue.current_policy: New runs default to independent Transformer-block Xavier initialization; old profiles without the key still use legacy initialization for checkpoint compatibility.
previous_initialization_issue.causality: No evidence yet that this explains the population-scale pilot failure. The two-ECG checks learned with both policies.

valid_design_choices_requiring_empirical: Learned random lead/time positional embeddings; the original image MAE uses fixed sin-cos position embeddings.
Global attention across lead-time tokens in the decoder.
Small encoder/decoder and a 1,000-update pilot training budget.
Final token LayerNorm followed by mean pooling for the frozen linear probe.

learning_rate_review.order: optimizer.step before scheduler.step; history.lr is next-update LR, history.lr_used is actual update LR when diagnostics are enabled

limits: Passing correctness tests does not establish optimal architecture or hyperparameters.
The added full-size forward/backward checks ran on local CPU, not the historical CUDA environment.
No new 5,000-ECG pretraining run or unseen-ECG generalization claim was made.
Input isolation is checked on the already preprocessed ECG tensors used by both backbones.
